subject: psychology
source_note: Topic structure follows the AQA GCSE Psychology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: Memory models are evaluated using the experimental methods studied in research methods
Perception research relies on controlled experiments and the variables defined in research methods
Classic obedience and conformity studies are case examples of the research designs taught here
Both are cognitive processes; stored memories shape how new sensory information is perceived
Theories of perceptual development explain how interpreting sensory input changes with age
Cognitive development depends on the maturation of brain structures studied in neuropsychology
Brain regions such as the hippocampus underpin the memory processes modelled cognitively
Biological explanations of depression and addiction draw on neurotransmission and brain function
Social context shapes how language and non-verbal communication develop and are used
Social factors and stigma influence the onset and treatment of depression and addiction
The link between language and thought connects to how we perceive and categorise the world
Language acquisition is a core strand of cognitive development
